_comment: Agentic Command Center - the single process dial. Hooks re-read this on every fire, so edits take effect immediately with no restart.

context._note: STANDING (2026-07-31, Kyle, set via the ACC dials + chat instruction; SUPERSEDES the 2026-07-30 100/150 standing): 400/600 until he manually changes it again. These dials are the ONLY source of context limits for EVERY session, ACC-launched or not - profiles carry no context overrides, so the number saved here is what budget.mjs enforces and statusline.mjs displays. softK MUST stay below hardK: budget.mjs returns allow() at 'ctx < softK*1000' before it ever tests hardK, so a softK above hardK silently disables the UserPromptSubmit and PostToolUse checks and leaves only the Stop hook. Measured baseline start context is ~35-42k (CLAUDE.md + memory index + tools). hardK is the TOTAL context ceiling, not headroom above baseline.

week._note: Tier counts usage from effectiveFrom onward (ACC install), so the switch cannot fire retroactively on pre-discipline burn. Baseline for reference: 2.35B tokens/7d before ACC. amber ~52% / red ~78% of that.

subagents._note: Implementation work belongs in a runner session (fresh context, cheap), not an Opus subagent. Multi-finder fan-out needs an explicit time-boxed grant: 'node hooks/budget.mjs fanout 30' or the Command Center Process tab.

rates._note: $ per million tokens, used for RELATIVE attribution in reports. These are list API prices, not subscription billing truth. Correct them here and every report follows.

autoClear._note: Outside watcher (watcher/clearbot.ps1) types /clear as real keystrokes when a session ends over hardK. Hooks cannot clear context themselves. false = fall back to telling Kyle to type it.

goals._note: A goal (runner/goals/) carries work across a /clear: SessionStart adopts it by CONSOLE PID and injects it, the Stop hook logs the cycle, clearbot types a constant to restart the turn. Kyle's call 2026-07-31: the loop ends only when the model runs 'goal.mjs done <id>' or 'blocked <id>' -- OR one of the ceilings below pauses it first (Phase 1, full-remediation-prompt.md, 2026-08-06: policy-only fix, zero code changes needed to roll back -- set all three ceilings to 0 and the pre-Phase-1 unbounded behavior reproduces exactly). maxCycles 12 / maxWallClockMinutes 180 / maxCostUsd 50 are generous-but-real: they exist to catch ONE runaway goal, not to bound normal work -- the pre-existing week kill switch is the coarser, whole-week brake this does not replace. onCeiling is currently informational only (the mechanism is always 'pause'; the key exists so a future stricter mode has somewhere to live without a schema change). A RED week tier holds all resumes regardless. Liveness (2026-07-31): a turn ending UNDER budget also re-arms the kick, so the loop no longer dies when a session simply finishes its turn - kickSettleSeconds is how long after a turn end a kick may fire, humanHoldMinutes is how long a prompt Kyle typed suppresses it (it expires, so walking away self-heals). A goal PAUSED at a ceiling: SessionStart warns instead of saying nothing, the status line shows 'goal PAUSED' while the alert is unread, and 'node hooks/goal.mjs resume <id>' re-arms it.

autoApprove._note: The Command Center runs pending runbox scripts itself instead of waiting for a human /approve (Kyle, 2026-07-31). Scripts marked [keep] are NEVER auto-run - they stay in the runbox after running, so auto-running them would loop forever. A failed script is attempted once per watcher lifetime and then left alone. Every run is appended to watcher/approvals.log. This does NOT touch the secrets list guard.mjs protects.

profiles._note: Chosen in the Command Center 'Start work' tab. The launcher sets ACC_PROFILE=<name>; budget.mjs and statusline.mjs (both via usage.mjs applyProfile) apply the SUBAGENT overrides for THAT SESSION only. Context limits ALWAYS come from the base dials above - single source of truth since 2026-07-31; do not add context blocks back here, they would shadow the Process-tab dials. Sessions with no ACC_PROFILE use the base policy unchanged.

Normal.label: The standard setup. Use this unless you have a reason not to.

Heavy.label: More helpers. For long migrations and audits.

autoCd._note: route.mjs blocks a prompt whose scope differs from cwd, writes a cd request, and the clearbot types /cd (plus /clear on a mid-session re-scope) then replays the prompt. enabled:false = advisory line only, no blocking and no typing. Set false 2026-08-04 (Kyle, guards OI-029) after repeated real prompts got blocked/eaten by stalled rescope cycles. Re-enabled 2026-08-04 (closing OI-029) now that OI-003 is RESOLVED: the root cause (clearbot's non-clear /cd settle delay, 1200ms hardcoded, too short) is fixed via the shared tui.readySettleMs dial above, real-token-verified (`node e2e/loop.e2e.mjs --only 4` PASS, cwd moved as expected). Watch for a recurrence before trusting this long-term.

tui._note: Single source of truth for 'how long after a session event until its Claude Code TUI is actually ready to accept injected input' -- shared by hooks/goal.mjs's kick (boundAt + this) and watcher/clearbot.ps1's Get-TuiReadyMs (the non-clear /cd settle, guards OI-003). Before 2026-08-05 these were two independently-guessed numbers (goal.mjs: 4000, proven via OI-002; clearbot.ps1: 1200, added for OI-003 and then failed a real-token repro on 2026-08-04) -- 4000 is the one with a track record, so it is now the only number and the default both readers fall back to. Lower it only with a real-token repro proving it still holds; clearbot's clear-branch settle and its post-cd replay/queuekick settles are deliberately NOT wired to this dial yet (unexamined, not proven broken -- see OI-003).

interactive._note: GUI Go button + Terminal tab (guards-gui.ps1). Own slot pool, isolated from automation's - pressing Go never queues behind a runner/e2e hold and vice versa. minGapMs:0 because a human clicking Go IS the pacing. breakerBlocking:false: a tripped breaker only warns an interactive launch (logged), never blocks it - a human who already decided to launch should not be queued behind automation's circuit breaker.

total._note: Machine-wide ceiling on concurrent claude.exe, enforced by shim/claude.cmd + shim/claude via `node hooks/lane.mjs gate` (see hooks/lane.mjs's launch-cap section). Independent of slots/interactive above, which are cooperative lane pools; this is a hard ceiling checked at every PATH resolution of `claude`, regardless of launch path. cap:0 is a supported deliberate lockdown (refuses every session launch). exe lists the absolute path(s) that count toward the cap, matched exactly (case-insensitive) -- the Claude desktop app's bundled claude.exe at a different path is never counted. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-claude-launch-cap-design.md.

lane._note: hooks/lane.mjs - machine-wide launch lane for real-claude spawns. Added 2026-08-01, hardened 2026-08-01 after Kyle hit an API error INSIDE an interactive session even after the first fix: the first pass only ever wrapped AUTOMATED headless launches (runner.mjs, e2e proof tier); guards-gui.ps1's Go button and Terminal tab spawned claude with zero coordination, so an interactive launch could still stack concurrently with automation or another manual terminal. slots=1 means one automated session at a time across ALL loops; minGapMs paces starts; retries are TRANSPORT-ONLY (econnreset/429/5xx/overloaded) with FULL-JITTER backoff - logic failures never retry, and 529/overloaded gets overloadBaseMs (a model-layer overload, not this account's rate limit) instead of backoffBaseMs. breakerThreshold failures within breakerWindowMs trips a breakerCooldownMs hold on new AUTOMATED launches (interactive only warns - see lane.interactive above). `lane.interactive` is a second, fully isolated slot pool for GUI/Terminal launches; `lane.total` (added 2026-08-03) is the machine-wide hard cap that catches launches neither of the above ever sees, e.g. Kyle's own manual terminals outside the GUI - see lane.total._note. State: os.tmpdir()/acc-lane, never ACC_ROOT.

tests._note: hooks/covgate.mjs floors, per CHANGED lib file (hooks/ and runner/ .mjs, tests exempt). Three floors because line coverage alone lies: V8 marks a declaration line covered even when the function is never called. Branches default 90 - the last branch points are defensive catch-paths needing fault injection; raise per-change when the file warrants the spend. hooks/testplan.mjs injects the contract that binds these gates at plan time. branchFloorOverrides keys are gate-relative paths (forward slashes) with a per-file changedBranchCoverage override - hooks/lane.mjs is overridden to 85% per OPEN-ISSUES.md OI-017: node's own --experimental-test-coverage merge under-reports its branches (measured 87.9%) once the full ten-file fast tier runs together in one invocation, a confirmed node v24.18.0 tooling limitation, not a real gap - true isolated coverage is 91.87%, proven 2026-08-02. kernel/run.mjs is overridden to 85% for the same reason, recurring on the CI covgate job's 24-file batch: measured 88.4% there vs 90.7% true isolated coverage (single-file, kernel/run.test.mjs only), proven 2026-08-03 after the timer-unref fix removed one optional-chaining branch point from the file.

kernel._note: kernel/ dials (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-acc-kernel-design.md). Re-read on EVERY guardhook fire, so an edit here applies to the next tool call with no restart. budget = per-run default ceilings; hardCaps.wallClockMin also bounds the task credential TTL; autonomy = rolling window of finalized runs, reject-rate trigger, tightening factor and how many runs it lasts; checkpointMin = automated re-evaluation interval, a run with zero tool calls in an interval is stopped as stalled. alwaysAllowTools are permitted regardless of contract (harmless bookkeeping tools). extraDenyWriteRoots adds to the built-in always-deny set (this repo + ~/.claude), never replaces it.
